chapter: Origins of jazz and the district
title: Barrelhouse music and slow drags explained
summary: Barrelhouse is slow bluesy piano with small groups; chatter about a visitor arriving.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You see? What was Barrel House? Huh? What was Barrel House music?

Oh, Barrel House, that's kind of hard to explain. It's a type of piano... All slow, more of the blues type, you know? And... Everything was dragged out. It was dragged out more or less in those days. And in fact, none of them had any what you'd call Dixieland combinations. Some of the places could only afford to have around two musicians, maybe a piano and drums. And the larger places, maybe they'd have six or seven men to them. But they'd never play the same type of music that we did for dancing. And they never played mazookas or charis or waltzes or reels and things like that there. See? But they didn't have... It was all slow, drag, bucket shop, a Barrel House and Bumpy music and things like that, too. Put the band in a... Put the people in a good yule. Give them time to get around the floor. They weren't in any hurry in the middle of the day, see? Yeah, he's your friend.
Come on. We'll be ready. We'll be ready.
He's driving. Is that your chauffeur?
I know it's your dinner time.
I know it's your dinner time and we're going to keep your mouth open.
